text.summary: Alkyl Amines Chemicals Limited’s Q4 and FY26 earnings conference call highlighted a year marked by flat revenue and profitability, with top-line and bottom-line growth remaining within ±1% of FY25 levels. Management attributed this to subdued market growth, though the company retained or slightly increased market share in key segments. Operational challenges arose in March due to ammonia supply disruptions caused by geopolitical tensions, but these were mitigated through inventory and improved sourcing. Ammonia prices surged from INR50/kg to over INR100/kg, prompting price hikes for finished goods, which were absorbed by customers due to the company’s products being minor cost components in their supply chains. Margins temporarily widened due to higher raw material costs and inventory advantages, but management expects competitive pressures to normalize margins over time. Volume growth for FY26 was flat to slightly negative (1% decline), with product-specific variations. A new project in Kurkumbh, delayed until Q2FY27, remains economically viable despite raw material and finished good price increases. Pharma (50-60% of sales) and agro (15-20%) sectors showed resilience, though agro faces El Niño-related monsoon concerns. Ethylamines capacity is sufficient for 4-5 years, while methylamines face overcapacity due to Aarti Industries’ new plant. R&D projects, including specialty chemicals for life sciences, are at various stages, with commercialization decisions deferred until market volatility stabilizes. Planned capex for FY27-FY28 is INR80-90 crores, focused on completing existing projects and maintenance. Green ammonia and coal gasification-derived methanol were discussed as long-term sourcing alternatives, though no immediate diversification plans were announced. Management expressed cautious optimism about future growth, citing reduced Chinese competition, improved margins, and potential demand from pharma and peptides sectors, though no specific growth targets were provided.
text.tone_note: Management balanced acknowledgment of operational challenges and market headwinds with cautious optimism about market share retention, margin recovery, and long-term growth drivers.
